Question 1 of 20, Level 1

1MCQCBSE SQP 2024-251 mark
A student observes an open-air honeybee nest on the branch of a tree, whose plane figure is parabolic in shape, given by x2=4yx^2 = 4yx2=4y. Then the area (in sq units) of the region bounded by the parabola x2=4yx^2 = 4yx2=4y and the line y=4y = 4y=4 is:

Tap the option you think is right.

Work it out on paper first. Then reveal the solution one step at a time.

Formula / idea Area between a curve and the y-axis: ∫cdx dy\displaystyle\int_c^d x\,dy∫cd​xdy

  1. 1

    Write xxx in terms of yyy (first quadrant)

    x2=4y⇒x=2yx^2 = 4y \Rightarrow x = 2\sqrt{y}x2=4y⇒x=2y​
  2. 2

    The region is symmetric about the y-axis, so double the first-quadrant part

    A=2∫042y dyA = 2\displaystyle\int_0^4 2\sqrt{y}\,dyA=2∫04​2y​dyA=2∫042y dy\displaystyle A = 2\displaystyle\int_0^4 2\sqrt{y}\,dyA=2∫04​2y​dy
  3. 3

    Integrate and put the limits

    A=4⋅23[y3/2]04=4⋅23⋅8=643A = 4\cdot\dfrac{2}{3}\left[y^{3/2}\right]_0^4 = 4 \cdot \dfrac{2}{3} \cdot 8 = \dfrac{64}{3}A=4⋅32​[y3/2]04​=4⋅32​⋅8=364​A=4⋅23[y3/2]04=4⋅23⋅8=643\displaystyle A = 4\cdot\dfrac{2}{3}\left[y^{3/2}\right]_0^4 = 4 \cdot \dfrac{2}{3} \cdot 8 = \dfrac{64}{3}A=4⋅32​[y3/2]04​=4⋅32​⋅8=364​
    1
Answer(B) 643\displaystyle \dfrac{64}{3}364​

Watch out Forgetting to double: the first-quadrant part alone is 323\dfrac{32}{3}332​, which is option (A).

Tap the option you think is right.

Work it out on paper first. Then reveal the solution one step at a time.

Formula / idea ∫a2−x2 dx=x2a2−x2+a22sin⁡−1xa+C\displaystyle\int \sqrt{a^2 - x^2}\,dx = \dfrac{x}{2}\sqrt{a^2 - x^2} + \dfrac{a^2}{2}\sin^{-1}\dfrac{x}{a} + C∫a2−x2​dx=2x​a2−x2​+2a2​sin−1ax​+C

  1. 1

    Radius r=6r = 6r=6; in the first quadrant the curve is

    y=36−x2,0≤x≤6y = \sqrt{36 - x^2},\quad 0 \le x \le 6y=36−x2​,0≤x≤6y=36−x2,0≤x≤6\displaystyle y = \sqrt{36 - x^2},\quad 0 \le x \le 6y=36−x2​,0≤x≤6
  2. 2

    Write the area

    A=∫0636−x2 dx=[x236−x2+18sin⁡−1x6]06A = \displaystyle\int_0^6 \sqrt{36 - x^2}\,dx = \left[\dfrac{x}{2}\sqrt{36 - x^2} + 18\sin^{-1}\dfrac{x}{6}\right]_0^6A=∫06​36−x2​dx=[2x​36−x2​+18sin−16x​]06​A=∫0636−x2 dx=[x236−x2+18sin⁡−1x6]06\displaystyle A = \displaystyle\int_0^6 \sqrt{36 - x^2}\,dx = \left[\dfrac{x}{2}\sqrt{36 - x^2} + 18\sin^{-1}\dfrac{x}{6}\right]_0^6A=∫06​36−x2​dx=[2x​36−x2​+18sin−16x​]06​
  3. 3

    Put the limits

    A=0+18⋅π2−0=9πA = 0 + 18 \cdot \dfrac{\pi}{2} - 0 = 9\piA=0+18⋅2π​−0=9πA=0+18⋅π2−0=9π\displaystyle A = 0 + 18 \cdot \dfrac{\pi}{2} - 0 = 9\piA=0+18⋅2π​−0=9π
    1
Answer(A) 9π\displaystyle 9\pi9π sq units

Watch out Giving the area of the whole circle, πr2=36π\pi r^2 = 36\piπr2=36π, when only one quadrant is asked.

Work it out on paper first. Then reveal the solution one step at a time.

    sin⁡x≥0\sin x \ge 0sinx≥0 on [0,π][0, \pi][0,π], so the area is the integral itself

    A=∫0πsin⁡x dxA = \displaystyle\int_0^{\pi} \sin x\,dxA=∫0π​sinxdxA=∫0πsin⁡x dx\displaystyle A = \displaystyle\int_0^{\pi} \sin x\,dxA=∫0π​sinxdx

    1
Answer(B) 2\displaystyle 22 sq units

Question 4Question 6

Question 6 of 20, Level 1

6Assertion-ReasonBoard-pattern1 mark
Assertion (A): The area of the region bounded by the curve y=x3y = x^3y=x3, the x-axis and the lines x=−1x = -1x=−1 and x=1x = 1x=1 is 000. Reason (R): ∫−11x3 dx=0\displaystyle\int_{-1}^{1} x^3\,dx = 0∫−11​x3dx=0, as x3x^3x3 is an odd function.

Tap the option you think is right.

Work it out on paper first. Then reveal the solution one step at a time.

Formula / idea Area is always positive: take the modulus of the part below the x-axis.

  1. 1

    For A: x3<0x^3 < 0x3<0 on (−1,0)(-1, 0)(−1,0), so split the area

    Area=∣∫−10x3 dx∣+∫01x3 dx=14+14=12\text{Area} = \left|\displaystyle\int_{-1}^{0} x^3\,dx\right| + \displaystyle\int_0^1 x^3\,dx = \dfrac{1}{4} + \dfrac{1}{4} = \dfrac{1}{2}Area=​∫−10​x3dx​+∫01​x3dx=41​+41​=21​Area=∣∫−10x3 dx∣+∫01x3 dx=14+14=12\displaystyle \text{Area} = \left|\displaystyle\int_{-1}^{0} x^3\,dx\right| + \displaystyle\int_0^1 x^3\,dx = \dfrac{1}{4} + \dfrac{1}{4} = \dfrac{1}{2}Area=​∫−10​x3dx​+∫01​x3dx=41​+41​=21​
  2. 2

    The area is 12\dfrac{1}{2}21​, not 000, so A is false

  3. 3

    For R: evaluate the integral

    ∫−11x3 dx=[x44]−11=14−14=0\displaystyle\int_{-1}^{1} x^3\,dx = \left[\dfrac{x^4}{4}\right]_{-1}^{1} = \dfrac{1}{4} - \dfrac{1}{4} = 0∫−11​x3dx=[4x4​]−11​=41​−41​=0∫−11x3 dx=[x44]−11=14−14=0\displaystyle \displaystyle\int_{-1}^{1} x^3\,dx = \left[\dfrac{x^4}{4}\right]_{-1}^{1} = \dfrac{1}{4} - \dfrac{1}{4} = 0∫−11​x3dx=[4x4​]−11​=41​−41​=0

    Integral of an odd function over [−a,a][-a, a][−a,a] is 000.

  4. 4

    So R is true; R cannot explain A, since A is false

  5. 5

    A is false and R is true, so the option is (D)

    1
Answer(D) A is false, but R is true

Watch out Taking the definite integral as the area; the two equal parts cancel in the integral.

    In the first quadrant, x=yx = \sqrt{y}x=y​; take horizontal strips from y=0y = 0y=0 to y=4y = 4y=4

Sketch the region bounded by the lines 2x+y=82x + y = 82x+y=8, y=2y = 2y=2, y=4y = 4y=4 and the y-axis. Hence, obtain its area using integration.

Work it out on paper first. Then reveal the solution one step at a time.

  1. 1

    Sketch: the line meets y=2y = 2y=2 at (3,2)(3, 2)(3,2) and y=4y = 4y=4 at (2,4)(2, 4)(2,4)

    1
  2. 2

    Write xxx in terms of yyy

    2x+y=8⇒x=8−y22x + y = 8 \Rightarrow x = \dfrac{8 - y}{2}2x+y=8⇒x=28−y​2x+y=8⇒x=8−y2\displaystyle 2x + y = 8 \Rightarrow x = \dfrac{8 - y}{2}2x+y=8⇒x=28−y​
  3. 3

    Take horizontal strips from y=2y = 2y=2 to y=4y = 4y=4

    A=∫24x dy=12∫24(8−y) dyA = \displaystyle\int_2^4 x\,dy = \dfrac{1}{2}\displaystyle\int_2^4 (8 - y)\,dyA=∫24​xdy=21​∫24​(8−y)dyA=∫24x dy=12∫24(8−y) dy\displaystyle A = \displaystyle\int_2^4 x\,dy = \dfrac{1}{2}\displaystyle\int_2^4 (8 - y)\,dyA=∫24​xdy=21​∫24​(8−y)dy
    1
  4. 4

    Integrate and put the limits

    A=12[8y−y22]24=12[(32−8)−(16−2)]A = \dfrac{1}{2}\left[8y - \dfrac{y^2}{2}\right]_2^4 = \dfrac{1}{2}\left[(32 - 8) - (16 - 2)\right]A=21​[8y−2y2​]24​=21​[(32−8)−(16−2)]A=12[8y−y22]24=12[(32−8)−(16−2)]\displaystyle A = \dfrac{1}{2}\left[8y - \dfrac{y^2}{2}\right]_2^4 = \dfrac{1}{2}\left[(32 - 8) - (16 - 2)\right]A=21​[8y−2y2​]24​=21​[(32−8)−(16−2)]
    ½
  5. 5

    Required area

    A=12×10=5 sq unitsA = \dfrac{1}{2} \times 10 = 5\ \text{sq units}A=21​×10=5 sq unitsA=12×10=5 sq units\displaystyle A = \dfrac{1}{2} \times 10 = 5\ \text{sq units}A=21​×10=5 sq units
    ½
Answer5\displaystyle 55 sq units

Watch out Using vertical strips with dxdxdx; the region is bounded by y=2y = 2y=2, y=4y = 4y=4 and the y-axis, so integrate w.r.t. yyy.

Work it out on paper first. Then reveal the solution one step at a time.

  1. 1

    Find where the line meets the x-axis (put y=0y = 0y=0)

    4−2x=0⇒x=24 - 2x = 0 \Rightarrow x = 24−2x=0⇒x=2
    ½
  2. 2

    Line is above the x-axis on [−1,2][-1, 2][−1,2] and below it on [2,3][2, 3][2,3]

    A=∫−12(4−2x) dx+∣∫23(4−2x) dx∣A = \displaystyle\int_{-1}^{2} (4 - 2x)\,dx + \left|\displaystyle\int_2^3 (4 - 2x)\,dx\right|A=∫−12​(4−2x)dx+​∫23​(4−2x)dx​A=∫−12(4−2x) dx+∣∫23(4−2x) dx∣\displaystyle A = \displaystyle\int_{-1}^{2} (4 - 2x)\,dx + \left|\displaystyle\int_2^3 (4 - 2x)\,dx\right|A=∫−12​(4−2x)dx+​∫23​(4−2x)dx​
    1
  3. 3

    First integral

    [4x−x2]−12=(8−4)−(−4−1)=9\left[4x - x^2\right]_{-1}^{2} = (8 - 4) - (-4 - 1) = 9[4x−x2]−12​=(8−4)−(−4−1)=9[4x−x2]−12=(8−4)−(−4−1)=9\displaystyle \left[4x - x^2\right]_{-1}^{2} = (8 - 4) - (-4 - 1) = 9[4x−x2]−12​=(8−4)−(−4−1)=9
    ½
  4. 4

    Second integral

    [4x−x2]23=(12−9)−(8−4)=−1\left[4x - x^2\right]_2^3 = (12 - 9) - (8 - 4) = -1[4x−x2]23​=(12−9)−(8−4)=−1[4x−x2]23=(12−9)−(8−4)=−1\displaystyle \left[4x - x^2\right]_2^3 = (12 - 9) - (8 - 4) = -1[4x−x2]23​=(12−9)−(8−4)=−1
    ½
  5. 5

    Required area

    A=9+∣−1∣=10 sq unitsA = 9 + |-1| = 10\ \text{sq units}A=9+∣−1∣=10 sq units
    ½
Answer10\displaystyle 1010 sq units

Watch out Integrating straight from −1-1−1 to 333 gives 9−1=89 - 1 = 89−1=8; the part below the x-axis must be added as ∣−1∣|-1|∣−1∣.

Using integration, find the area of the minor segment of the circle x2+y2=16x^2 + y^2 = 16x2+y2=16 cut off by the line x=2x = 2x=2.

  1. 1

    The line x=2x = 2x=2 meets the circle at (2,±23)(2, \pm 2\sqrt{3})(2,±23​); the minor segment runs from x=2x = 2x=2 to x=4x = 4x=4

  2. 2

    The segment is symmetric about the x-axis

    A=2∫2416−x2 dxA = 2\displaystyle\int_2^4 \sqrt{16 - x^2}\,dxA=2∫24​16−x2​dxA=2∫2416−x2 dx\displaystyle A = 2\displaystyle\int_2^4 \sqrt{16 - x^2}\,dxA=2∫24​16−x2​dx

Question 20 of 20, Level 3

20Case studyBoard-pattern4 marks
Case Study: A circular garden in a housing society has its boundary given by x2+y2=100x^2 + y^2 = 100x2+y2=100, with its centre at the origin (units in metres). A flower bed is to be made in the part of the garden between two straight paths along the lines x=−5x = -5x=−5 and x=5x = 5x=5. Based on this information, answer the following questions using integration.
  1. (i)Find the total area of the garden.1 mark
  2. (ii)Find the area of the part of the garden lying in the first quadrant.1 mark
  3. (iii)Find the area of the flower bed, that is, the part of the garden between the lines x=−5x = -5x=−5 and x=5x = 5x=5.2 marks

Work it out on paper first. Then reveal the solution one step at a time.

Formula / idea ∫a2−x2 dx=x2a2−x2+a22sin⁡−1xa+C\displaystyle\int \sqrt{a^2 - x^2}\,dx = \dfrac{x}{2}\sqrt{a^2 - x^2} + \dfrac{a^2}{2}\sin^{-1}\dfrac{x}{a} + C∫a2−x2​dx=2x​a2−x2​+2a2​sin−1ax​+C

(i)1 mark

Answer (i)100π m2\displaystyle 100\pi\ \text{m}^2100π m2
